plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 (24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 dual-band stack) based on feedback directives. Four complementary routes: (1) Direct implementation of feedback-specified thickness seed re-initialization with reduced optimizer step size; (2) Layer count expansion from 24 to 28 layers to test additional degrees of freedom; (3) Quarter-wave initialization at 300 nm center for UV band as physically-motivated starting point; (4) Constrained local refinement around iteration_05 best candidate with symmetric ±10 nm bounds to test whether narrow exploration improves robustness. All routes maintain HfO2/SiO2 material restriction, fused silica substrate, and ≤30 layer constraint.

routes.title: Transition-Zone Seed Re-initialization with Damped Optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Compressing layers 1-3 to 40-60 nm and expanding layers 5-8 to 100-140 nm will sharpen the spectral roll-off between UV reflection (200-400 nm) and SWIR transmission (800-1500 nm) bands, improving dual-band separation compared to uniform 100 nm initialization.
routes.design_principle: Targeted thickness seed perturbation in the spectral transition zone (layers controlling the 400-800 nm transition region) combined with reduced optimizer step size to dampen oscillations around the current configuration.
routes.proposed_topology: 24-layer alternating stack: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate
design_variables: Thickness bounds: layers 1-3: 40-60 nm, layers 5-8: 100-140 nm, remaining layers: 30-200 nm
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 200-400 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Absolute thickness tolerance ±15 nm for robustness analysis
theory_basis: Feedback directive specifies transition-zone focused re-initialization to sharpen spectral roll-off
Non-quarter-wave optimization allows finer spectral control than fixed quarter-wave stacks
expected_advantages: Sharper spectral transition between UV rejection and SWIR transmission bands
Reduced optimizer oscillation due to 20% step size reduction
Better exploitation of iteration_05 configuration knowledge
known_risks: Overly narrow seed ranges may trap optimizer in local minimum
Layer 4 boundary effects between compressed and expanded regions may create unintended interference
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack on fused silica substrate for dual-band performance. Incidence: air, normal angle, unpolarized. Materials: HfO2 (high-index), SiO2 (low-index). Layer sequence: HfO2/SiO2 alternating, starting with HfO2. Thickness bounds: layers 1-3: 40-60 nm, layers 5-8: 100-140 nm, layers 4 and 9-24: 30-200 nm. Initialize with perturbed seeds in specified ranges. Objectives: maximize mean transmittance 800-1500 nm, maximize mean reflectance 200-400 nm. Optimizer: gradient_thickness with step size reduced 20% from baseline. Robustness: ±15 nm absolute normal deviation. Total layer count fixed at 24. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 200-400 nm, 800-1500 nm. soft objectives: High transmission in 800-1500 nm band; High reflection in 200-400 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low transmission in 200-400 nm band; Low reflection in 800-1500 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layers <= 30; Materials limited to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Direct implementation of feedback directive: re-initialize population with perturbed thickness seeds focused on spectral transition zone (compress layers 1-3 to 40-60 nm, expand layers 5-8 to 100-140 nm), reduce optimizer step size by 20% to dampen oscillations.

routes.title: Layer Count Expansion to 28 Layers
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Expanding from 24 to 28 layers provides additional degrees of freedom for spectral shaping, enabling better simultaneous optimization of UV reflection and SWIR transmission within the 30-layer manufacturing constraint.
routes.design_principle: Incremental layer count increase tests whether additional optical thickness enables improved dual-band performance, leveraging evidence that multi-wavelength high-reflectors often require 30+ layers for complex spectral targets.
routes.proposed_topology: 28-layer alternating stack: Air | (HfO2 | SiO2) x14 | Fused Silica substrate
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 200-400 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Increased deposition time and complexity vs 24-layer design
theory_basis: Evidence shows 38-layer TiO2/SiO2 HR achieved >99.99% reflectance at multiple wavelengths
79-layer HfO2/SiO2 tri-band HR demonstrates layer count enables complex spectral control
expected_advantages: Additional 4 layers provide more interference control points
Potential for sharper band edges and higher UV reflectance
Closer to 30-layer manufacturing limit allows testing boundary performance
known_risks: Increased layer count may not yield proportional performance gain
More variables may slow optimizer convergence
Deposition complexity and stress accumulation increase with layer count

routes.title: Quarter-Wave Initialization at 300 nm UV Center
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses at quarter-wave optical thickness for 300 nm (UV band center) provides a physically-motivated starting point that converges faster to high UV reflectance solutions than uniform 100 nm seeds.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stack theory provides known high-reflectance starting configuration; HfO2 ~50 nm and SiO2 ~75 nm at 300 nm center wavelength establishes strong UV reflectance baseline for subsequent optimization.
routes.proposed_topology: 24-layer alternating stack: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate

soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 200-400 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Quarter-wave thicknesses well within deposition control capabilities
theory_basis: Evidence shows quarter-wave HfO2/SiO2 stacks achieve 99.5% reflectance at design wavelength
DBR theory: alternating high/low index at quarter-wave optical thickness maximizes reflectance at center wavelength
expected_advantages: Physically-motivated initialization may avoid poor local minima

300 nm QW thicknesses may not optimize 800-1500 nm transmission band

routes.title: Constrained Local Refinement Around Iteration_05 Best
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Constraining thickness search to ±10 nm around iteration_05 best candidate (target_score 0.74) will improve robustness score by focusing optimization on local refinement rather than broad exploration.
routes.design_principle: Local refinement around known good solution tests whether narrow search bounds yield higher manufacturing robustness than wide-range optimization, trading exploration depth for solution stability.
